spec.body_markdown:
## Accuracy

Accuracy describes how close a measured value is to the actual, true value of the quantity being measured.

- You need to know the true (or accepted) value to judge accuracy.
- A measurement is accurate when it is close to this true value, regardless of how many decimal places it has.
- Example: if water boils at 100°C and your thermometer reads 99.8°C, the reading is accurate. A reading of 115°C is not.
- Accuracy is different from precision, which is about consistency rather than correctness.
